assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuinely new observational window: a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector built in Antarctic ice that detected astrophysical neutrinos and then identified sources (the TXS 0506+056 blazar, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane). It is detector development leading to discovery, which I weigh heavily, and it will last as neutrino astronomy.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove IceCube; Karle and Spiering were central to construction, the AMANDA precursor and the collaboration's analysis. This is a plausible three-person configuration, though a large collaboration means the line between instrument leadership and analysis leadership needs care.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is strong: the diffuse flux is seen in several channels, and the source evidence has been followed up with multi-wavelength data. Timing looks right, since the discovery dates to 2013 and the source identifications to 2018-2023.
uncertainties: Whether the neutrino-source identifications (TXS, NGC 1068) are firm enough, since statistical significance is moderate.
Whether credit should go to the IceCube leadership or also to the predecessor experiments (AMANDA, Baikal, ANTARES) and the theorists who set the target flux.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and Ye's group took it to systematic uncertainty near 1e-18. This opens a measurement regime with uses in fundamental physics and geodesy. Precision metrology is a tradition I respect, though atomic physics is outside my own expertise and I would lean on colleagues.
assessment.attribution: The two-person configuration is clean: Katori has the invention and the first realisation, Ye the leading accuracy and stability results. Hall and Hänsch (2005) and Wineland (2012) were rewarded for related work, which marginally reduces the novelty, but the invention is distinct.
assessment.maturity: Many independent labs have reproduced optical lattice clocks and the progress is reliable. The redefinition of the SI second is still pending, but the science is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier combs and ion-clock prizes in the committee's view.
Whether the contribution of the other early lattice-clock groups warrants a third name; the supplied credit does not include one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proposals for quantum gates with trapped ions and for neutral-atom simulation and computation laid the theoretical blueprint for much of present quantum technology, and experiments have since realised them in several platforms. Impact is large and durable, but the discipline is outside my own expertise.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the evident pair for the foundational proposals, and it is a clean two-person credit. Experimental work (Wineland, Blatt, Monroe) is partly rewarded or is not part of this credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the ion and atom platforms have confirmed the proposals over about thirty years, and the technology is now being scaled. Recognition is not premature, though the 2012 and 2025 prizes are nearby.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for ion control and with the 2025 quantum-technology prize, which the committee may see as already covering the area.
Theory versus experiment balance: the experimental implementations are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision CMB anisotropy mapping with WMAP established the standard cosmological model with percent-level parameters. It is a large, space-borne instrument achievement and I know well the calibration and systematics work behind it. It is also an observational discipline I am comfortable evaluating.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led WMAP, Page was a key instrument scientist and Spergel led the cosmological analysis. Planck's contributions (Puget and the HFI team) are real and make a credit assignment with three names difficult.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed by Planck and by ground- and balloon-based experiments over two decades. Not premature, though COBE (2006) already rewarded the CMB, so the committee may feel part of the field has been honoured.
uncertainties: Competition for credit between WMAP and Planck and between instrument and analysis roles.
Whether the 2006 COBE prize and the 2019 cosmology prize reduce appetite for further CMB recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon pixel detectors made precise vertexing and tracking at LHC-scale rates possible and underpin the Higgs, heavy-flavour and top results, as well as imaging uses. This is an instrument invention of clear lasting value, and it would be a first for detector technology in several decades, but a pixel concept has several sub-lineages.
assessment.attribution: Heijne (hybrid pixels), Parker (planar and 3D silicon) and Snoeys (monolithic CMOS) represent different branches of a technique developed by many groups, including the CERN RD19 and Medipix communities. A three-person credit is defensible but incomplete, and I should expect disagreement within the committee.
assessment.maturity: Technology is proven in every LHC experiment and in X-ray imaging, so it is long mature; the open issue is whether the prize wants the detector rather than the physics it enabled.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over many contributors and technology generations, and attribution may not be crisp.
The committee tradition is less used to rewarding detector technology as such.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* via global VLBI are a major measurement achievement that tests general relativity in the strong field, built on a new coordinated instrument. Importance is high and it speaks to the public in an obvious way.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging idea, Doeleman led the EHT's instrument and collaboration and Moran contributed the foundational VLBI technology. Credit is spread over a collaboration of hundreds and a consistent three-person choice is contested.
assessment.maturity: Two sources imaged and polarisation and multi-epoch results are accumulating, but independent confirmation by other arrays is still limited and the interpretation of the ring structure depends on modelling. Slightly early.
uncertainties: Dependence on imaging and modelling choices (priors, calibration) and the absence of a fully independent confirmation.
Large-collaboration credit and the 2020 black-hole prize already given to Penrose, Genzel and Ghez.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84 and E91) is a conceptually original use of quantum mechanics for secure communication, with experimental realisations and commercial and satellite links. Impact is real, though the practical security record is mixed and I rely on colleagues for the quantum-information side.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the BB84 originators and Ekert independently proposed entanglement-based QKD. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea and the later experimental work are not credited, and the 2022 prize touched entanglement tests.
assessment.maturity: Principle is well established and implemented over fibre and satellites, but practical deployment and side-channel security remain limited and evolving. Timely, though the 2022 and 2025 prizes are close.
uncertainties: Wiesner's priority and the deceased co-originators of the idea.
Whether the committee views QKD as physics or as information technology, and overlap with the 2022 entanglement prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens the gravitational-wave spectrum beyond LIGO's band and rests on decades of precision timing. It is a patient, calibration-heavy measurement of a kind I respect.
assessment.attribution: Kramer, Manchester and McLaughlin are leaders of the PPTA, EPTA and NANOGrav efforts respectively, but the key results come from several collaborations that analysed the data jointly, so this is a natural but partial grouping.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 evidence is about 3-4 sigma and interpretation (supermassive black-hole binaries or new physics) is unsettled, so the result is premature compared with the other candidates, though it will probably mature.
uncertainties: Significance below the discovery threshold and the unsettled astrophysical origin.
Credit across at least four collaborations and the individuals named, which supports a prize only if the committee is comfortable with a simplified allocation.
